title: Protocol for morphometric analysis of neurons derived from human pluripotent stem cells
protocol: Plate 3 × 10^4 NSCs per cm² in NSC medium in one well of a 6-well cell culture plate pretreated with 1 mL of 1/100 Geltrex for 1 h at 37°C.
Remove 2.5 mL of NSC medium from the well of a 6-well plate on day 0.
Wash with 1 mL of warm (37°C) PBS 1×.
Add 2.5 mL of neuronal differentiation medium to the well on day 0.
Change to 2.5 mL of fresh medium every other day on days 2-4.
Replate cells on day 6.
Remove 2.5 mL of Neuronal differentiation medium from the well.
Wash with 1 mL of warm (37°C) DPBS 1× containing calcium and magnesium.
Incubate cells with 500 μL of Accutase 1× for 7 min at 37°C.
Dilute Accutase 1× with 1 mL of DPBS 1× containing calcium and magnesium.
Gently detach and transfer cells into a 15 mL conical tube using a pipette.
Centrifuge cells at 200 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Prepare a 0.4% solution of Trypan blue in buffered isotonic salt solution (PBS).
Centrifuge an aliquot of cell suspension being tested for viability 5 min at 200 × g.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet by pipetting up and down 10 times in 1 mL PBS.
Add 0.1 mL of Trypan blue stock solution to 0.1 mL of cell suspension.
Pipette up and down to thoroughly mix the two solutions.
Allow mixture to incubate ∼3 min at 20°C–25°C.
Count the unstained (viable) and stained (non-viable) cells separately in the hemocytometer.
Plate 7 × 10^5 cells per well in a 12-well cell culture plate pretreated with 1 mL Geltrex (1/100).
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Gently pipette and thoroughly disaggregate cell clumps into single-cell suspension, avoiding bubble formation when pipetting.
Change Neuronal differentiation medium to 2.5 mL of fresh medium every other day from Day 8 to Day 11.
On Day 12, change the medium to 2.5 mL of Neuronal differentiation medium without antibiotics.
Dilute 4 μL of Lipofectamine Stem Transfection Reagent in 50 μL of Neuronal differentiation medium without antibiotics on Day 13.
Dilute 500 ng of DNA plasmid in 50 μL of Neuronal differentiation medium without antibiotics on Day 13.
Add diluted DNA to the diluted lipofectamine and mix by pipetting, avoiding bubble formation.
Incubate the mixed solution for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Remove the medium from the well and add 900 μL of Neuronal differentiation medium without antibiotics.
Mix gently by pipetting the DNA-lipofectamine complexes.
Add the DNA-lipofectamine complexes to the wells.
Incubate for 12–16 hours at 37°C in 5% CO2.
Change medium containing lipofectamine with 2.5 mL of fresh Neuronal differentiation medium.
If high toxicity is observed, change the medium with lipofectamine for fresh medium after 4–6 hours of addition.
Add Hoechst (1 μg/mL final concentration) and incubate for 15 min to visualize nuclei.
Use another type of cell-permeable stain that marks living cells if not using Hoechst.
Visualize and photograph transfected neurons using an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Perform immunofluorescence staining for neuronal markers such as βIII-tubulin/TUJ-1, Microtubule-associated protein 2/MAP-2, and Microtubule-associated protein 5/MAP-5.
Calibrate the FIJI software with the measurements in micrometers for the photographs.
Photograph a Neubauer chamber using the same objective as for neuron images.
Load the Neubauer chamber photograph using the file button in the MENU BAR and then select “Open…” from the sub-menu.
Trace a line between two points using the “straight” tool from the TOOL bar.
Select the Analyze button from the MENU BAR and choose Set Scale… from the sub-menu.
Set the scale with the known distance of 50 μm, which corresponds to the width of the squares in the center of the counting chamber.
Check the “global” box to apply the scale parameters to all uploaded photos.
Load GFP-transfected neurons and Hoechst-stained nuclei images using the file button in the MENU BAR.
Select “Open…” from the sub-menu to load the images.
Use images showing Hoechst-stained blue nuclei to distinguish the soma of the neurons.
Work with images showing the expression of GFP in transfected cells neurons.
Mark the area corresponding to the neural body with the polygon selection tool from the TOOLS MENU.
Analyze from MENU BAR.
Select Measure from the sub-menu.
A new window would appear to determine the area of the neuronal soma in μm².
Save this quantification in a file.
Open the Simple Neurite Tracer plugin from the Plugin button in MENU BAR.
Mark the start and end of the main neurite.
End the pathway to observe the length of the prolongation in micrometers.
Mark “yes” if the parts are well connected.
Click the “finish path” button if all the neurite is marked.
Make the same procedure for secondary neurites.
Incubate a 96-well conical V bottom plate with Anti-Adherent Rising Solution (30 μL per well) at 20°C–25°C for 30 min.
Maintain NSCs in optimal conditions with good morphology.
Remove 2.5 mL of medium from a well of a 6-well plate.
Wash NSCs with 1 mL of warm (37°C) DPBS 1× with calcium and magnesium.
Incubate NSCs with 500 μL of Accutase 1× for 7 min at 37°C.
Dilute Accutase 1× with 1 mL of DPBS 1× with calcium and magnesium.
Gently detach and transfer cells into a 15 mL conical tube using a pipette.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of NSCs medium.
Count the cell number with your preferred method.
Plate 8000 NSCs in each well of a 96-well plate in a final volume of 100 μL.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate at 200 × g for 5 min.
Incubate the plated cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Remove NSCs medium from the wells.
Wash carefully with 150 μL of warm (37°C) DPBS 1× with calcium and magnesium.
Add 150 μL of Neuronal differentiation medium to each well.
Change the medium every other day by removing 130 μL and replacing it with fresh medium.
Tilt the plate at a 45-degree angle toward you and slowly remove the medium touching the wall of the well without reaching the bottom where the neurosphere is placed.
Leave approximately 20 μL of medium to cover the neurospheres.
Change the medium in turns, alternating with 37°C incubations (i.e., change 24 wells per turn for a total of 4 times).
Use a p200 pipette with a 10 μL tip at its end for greater precision when removing the medium.
On day 11 of neuronal differentiation, transfer neurospheres from a 96-well plate to a 48-well cell culture plate pretreated with Geltrex at 37°C for 1 hour.
Add 300 μL of Neuronal differentiation medium per well of the 48-well plate and warm it at 37°C.
Remove the medium from the 96-well plate and add 50 μL of fresh medium.
Use a sterile cut P1000 tip to transfer neurospheres carefully from the 96-well conical V bottom plate to each well of the 48-well cell culture plate without damaging them.
Plate 1–2 individual neurospheres per well, excluding any that stick together.
Change the medium every other day to a final volume of 400 μL per each well of the 48-well cell culture plate until day 14 of the neuronal differentiation protocol.
Mark the location where the neurospheres were adhered to the plate with a marker.
Remove the medium from each well using a p200 pipette fitted with a 10 μL tip for precision.
Wash the wells with 200 μL warm (37°C) DPBS containing magnesium and calcium.
Fix cells with 200 μL Fixation Immunostaining Solution for 15 min at 20°C–25°C.
Store neurospheres in 400 μL of Washing Immunostaining Solution per well of a 48-well plate at 4°C for up to 2 weeks.
Wash neurospheres with 200 μL of Washing Immunostaining Solution for 5 minutes.
Repeat the previous washing step twice.
Permeate neurospheres with 200 μL of Permeabilization Immunostaining Solution for 45 minutes.
Incubate neurospheres with 50 μL of Anti-tubulin β3 (TUJ-1) primary antibody at a dilution of 1:1000 in Permeabilization Immunostaining Solution for 12–16 hours at 4°C without agitation or shaking.
Wash neurospheres with 200 μL of Washing Immunostaining Solution for 5 minutes.
Repeat the previous washing step twice.

Incubate neurospheres with 50 μL of a secondary antibody recognizing primary antibody heavy chain (Alexa 488, diluted at 1:400 in Permeabilization Immunostaining Solution) for 45 minutes at 20°C–25°C protected from light.
Wash neurospheres with 200 μL of Washing Immunostaining Solution for 5 minutes.
Repeat the previous washing step twice.
Place 400 μL of Washing Immunostaining Solution per well of a 48-well plate.
Observe the neurospheres under a fluorescence microscope.
Open FIJI software.
Load images of TUJ-1 immunostained neurospheres using the file button in the MENU BAR and then select “Open…” from the sub-menu.
Select the area corresponding to the neurosphere with the polygon selection tool from the TOOLS MENU.
Choose Analyze from MENU BAR and select “Set measurements…” from the sub-menu to tick area and perimeter boxes.
Select Analyze from MENU BAR and click Measure from the sub-menu.
Use the polygon tool to quantify the area and perimeter of a neurosphere.
Delimit the edge of the neurosphere through the junction of the neurites.
Save the quantification in a file.
